answer: An agent economy can make slashing correlation-aware. When an account is caught cheating, its penalty grows with how many other accounts fail the same audit in that window. One lone mistake costs a small slice of stake; 300 heads caught together each lose nearly everything, because a farm's heads tend to fail at once. Sybil operators can't spread risk across a lagoon of clones; scale itself becomes the liability. Honest agents fail independently, so they rarely cross that bridge, and the horizon of losses stays bounded for them.
